assays.assay_description: Transparent cages with ~4.5 cm fine sawdust and 20 glass marbles in a 5×4 pattern; 30-min session under dim light; marbles ≥2/3 covered counted. Drug-free pretest used for selection (≥15 marbles); drug test ≥1 week later 30 min after i.p. psilocybin ± M100907, 8-OH-DPAT, WAY100635, buspirone (escitalopram positive control). Subset retested at 7 days; staggered psilocybin dosing (4 × 1.1 mg/kg) also tested.

application_type.evidence: Drugs were administered by intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection in a standard injection volume of 300 µl 30 min before the MBT.

setup_habituation.evidence: No habituation without data collection described; the pretest was a data-collecting selection session.

setup_restrain.evidence: The mice were left in the cage with the marbles for a 30-min period.

food_restriction.evidence: Test cages contained sawdust and marbles only; no food is described in the test cage.

water_restriction.evidence: No water is described in the test cage.

time_to_assay.evidence: 30 min before the MBT; persistence retest 7 days following the initial MBT

sample_size.evidence: n = 8-16 (Fig. 1); n = 15-17 (Fig. 2); persistence: vehicle n = 5, psilocybin n = 4; staggered: vehicle n = 6, psilocybin n = 9

outcomes.summary: Acute psilocybin 4.4 mg/kg reduced marble burying by 32.84% vs vehicle, comparable to escitalopram. The effect was not blocked by M100907 or WAY100635. It was additive with 8-OH-DPAT but not with buspirone. The effect was absent at the 7-day retest and when the dose was given in staggered injections.
outcomes.statistics: Psilocybin vs VEH p = 0.001; Fig. 1 one-way ANOVA F6,56 = 15.33, p < 0.0001; psilocybin main effect F1,40 = 24.8, p < 0.0001; M100907 F1,40 = 7.7, p = 0.008; psilocybin F1,37 = 10.4, p = 0.0026; DPAT F1,37 = 74.3, p < 0.0001; interaction F1,37 = 0.9, p = 0.34; Fig. 2 F6,105 = 6.045, p < 0.0001; psilocybin F1,61 = 42.47, p < 0.0001; WAY F1,61 = 0.4, p = 0.521; interaction F1,61 = 0.0003, p = 0.985; buspirone × psilocybin F1,75 = 5.805, p = 0.018; persistence p = 0.53; staggered p > 0.10
outcomes.evidence: Mice administered psilocybin buried 32.84% fewer marbles over 30 min than vehicle-treated mice (p = 0.001, Fig. 1)... No significant effect of psilocybin was observed (vehicle 18.6 ± 1.6, n = 5; psilocybin 17.75 ± 2.21, n = 4; p = 0.53).

B1_num_measures.evidence: the number of buried marbles was counted after 30 min

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Only the end-of-session count at 30 min was reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: the marble-burying test (MBT) uses the propensity of rodents to dig and cover non-threatening objects (digging is a natural repertoire behaviour)

B5_social.evidence: Non-social test; mice tested alone in a cage.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Innate digging/burying behaviour; no learning required.

E1_environment_type.evidence: MBT was performed in transparent cages containing ~4.5 cm fine sawdust

E2_shelter.evidence: No shelter described in the test cage.

E3_bedding.evidence: transparent cages containing ~4.5 cm fine sawdust

E5_enrichment.evidence: Marbles are the test stimuli, not enrichment.

E7_social_context.evidence: The mice were left in the cage with the marbles for a 30-min period (no conspecific described).

E8_food_water.evidence: No food/water described in the test cage.

D1_continuity.evidence: All mice underwent a pretest without any injection, and the number of marbles buried was counted... the definitive experiment, which took place at least a week following the pretest; subset retested 7 days later.

D2_session_duration.evidence: The mice were left in the cage with the marbles for a 30-min period

D3_recording_days.evidence: Pretest day, drug test day (≥1 week later), and 7-day retest in a subset = 3 recording days.

D4_baseline.evidence: All mice underwent a pretest without any injection, and the number of marbles buried was counted.

D5_followup.evidence: We examined marble burying in a subset of mice treated with vehicle or psilocybin 7 days following the initial MBT.

assays.assay_description: Square wooden arena (50 × 50 × 40 cm, white walls, black floor). Run immediately after the MBT (~60 min post-injection) for 30 min. Total distance, centre duration and periphery duration tracked with EthoVision XT-12.

application_type.evidence: Drugs were administered by intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection... 30 min before the MBT. The OFT was performed immediately after the MBT

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were placed individually in the center of the open field and allowed to freely explore the apparatus for 30 min.

food_restriction.evidence: No food described in the open-field arena.

water_restriction.evidence: No water described in the open-field arena.

time_to_assay.evidence: Our activity measurements were not performed during the MBT, 30-60 min after the psilocybin injection but after the MBT, 60-90 min after psilocybin administration.

sample_size.evidence: not reported (Supplementary Fig. 1 legend not available)

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin and buspirone did not alter total distance travelled, centre duration or periphery duration vs vehicle. This suggests the reduced marble burying was not due to motor suppression.
outcomes.evidence: there was no significant difference in distance traveled between vehicle-treated mice and those administered psilocybin or buspirone. Similarly, there was no difference in time spent by the mice in the center... or in the periphery of the open field

B1_num_measures.evidence: distance traveled... center duration... periphery duration (3 measures)

B4_ethological.evidence: Locomotor distance and zone times are spatial measures.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Ethovision XT-12 Video Tracking System (position tracking; score-0 list)

E1_environment_type.evidence: square wooden arena (50 × 50 × 40 cm) with white walls and a black floor

E7_social_context.evidence: Mice were placed individually in the center of the open field

D1_continuity.evidence: monitored for 30 min on completion of the MBT

D2_session_duration.evidence: allowed to freely explore the apparatus for 30 min

D3_recording_days.evidence: Performed once, immediately after the MBT.

assays.assay_description: Neodymium magnets attached to the outer ears. Mice were placed in a magnetometer apparatus immediately after i.p. vehicle, psilocybin 4.4 mg/kg, buspirone 5 mg/kg, or the combination. HTR was recorded for 20 min at 1000 Hz and processed with custom MATLAB/GUI. Both the time course and total HTR were analysed.

application_type.evidence: placed inside a magnetometer apparatus... immediately after injection of vehicle or psilocybin 4.4 mg/kg (drugs administered i.p.)

setup_habituation.evidence: Only a 5- to 7-day post-surgical recovery period is described, not apparatus habituation.

setup_restrain.evidence: the ear-tagged animals were placed inside a magnetometer apparatus; no restraint described (magnets on ears only)

food_restriction.evidence: No food described in magnetometer apparatus.

water_restriction.evidence: No water described in magnetometer apparatus.

time_to_assay.evidence: placed inside a magnetometer apparatus... immediately after injection

sample_size.evidence: n = 6-12 (Tukey's multiple comparisons test); F3,32 implies 36 animals across 4 groups

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin 4.4 mg/kg significantly increased HTR over 20 min vs vehicle. Co-administration of buspirone 5 mg/kg blocked this increase. Time-course analysis showed significant time × psilocybin × buspirone interactions.
outcomes.statistics: Time F9,288 = 5.001, p = 0.0032; Time × psilocybin F9,288 = 3.224, p = 0.001; Time × psilocybin × buspirone F9,288 = 2.687, p = 0.0072; psilocybin F1,32 = 19.22, p = 0.0001; buspirone F1,32 = 7.483, p = 0.0101; psilocybin × buspirone F1,32 = 5.237, p = 0.0289; total HTR F3,32 = 12.87, p < 0.0001; psilocybin vs vehicle p < 0.001; buspirone + psilocybin vs psilocybin p = 0.0009
outcomes.evidence: In post-hoc tests, there was a significant effect of psilocybin to increase HTR compared to vehicle (p < 0.001), while buspirone and buspirone + psilocybin effects were significantly lower than the effect of psilocybin (p = 0.0002 and p = 0.0009, respectively).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Head twitch count (time-binned and total over 20 min) is a single variable

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Three-way ANOVA with repeated measures showed a significant within-subjects effect of time... reflecting the changes in HTR rate during the course of the test

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR is excluded from ethological behaviours per rubric.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Magnetometer signal processed by custom MATLAB script; not pose estimation or an ML behavioural classifier.

judge_notes: All three candidates identified the same three assays (MBT, OFT, HTR). The 7-day persistence retest and the staggered-dosing experiment were collapsed into the single MBT assay per the rubric's same-paradigm rule.
MBT B4 set to Yes (deepseek and gemma vs qwen): the rubric explicitly lists digging as ethological.
MBT D2 set to 15–60 min (30-min session). Gemma's '<15 min' contradicts its own evidence.
OFT B1 set to score 1 / '2-3' for three measures (distance, centre, periphery). Deepseek's '4-6' and gemma's score 2 are inconsistent with the rubric.
HTR B1 set to score 0: the time-course and total HTR are the same variable. HTR D2 set to 15–60 min (20 min), overriding gemma.
HTR setup_restrain set to 'no' (modal); setup_habituation set to not_reported, since the 5–7 day recovery period is not apparatus habituation.
MBT setup_habituation set to not_reported: the pretest collected data and is scored as a baseline (D4), not as habituation.
HTR time_dependent set to n/a per the rubric (n/a unless time_to_assay = multiple). Within-session time effects are captured in B2.
Age set to not_reported (only body weight is given); I did not adopt the inferred 'adult' value.
HTR n_total of 36 is derived from F3,32 degrees of freedom.
Dosing expanded to list all compounds administered. The psilocybin staggered 1.1 mg/kg × 4 regimen is noted in doses.
MBT n_per_group_min of 4 comes from the persistence subset.
